name: Rippling
description: Rippling HR platform: workers and users, departments, teams, work locations, levels, titles, employment types, custom fields, compensation, leave types, balances and requests, supergroups and time entries. Rippling REST API with an API token.
prerequisites: A Rippling user with permission to create API tokens (Developer app, API credentials) and access to the data the agent should read.

RIPPLING_API_TOKEN.label: API token
RIPPLING_API_TOKEN.help: Rippling, Developer > API credentials > New API token. Select the scopes of the tools you use (companies.read at least). The value is shown only once.
RIPPLING_API_TOKEN.patternMessage: Paste only the token, without Bearer, spaces or quotes.

verifyHints.401: Rippling refused the token. It may be revoked, mistyped, or expired: tokens unused for 30 days and tokens of terminated owners are revoked. Create a new one under Developer > API credentials.
verifyHints.403: The token lacks a scope (companies.read for the check) or its owner's permission profile does not cover the data. Edit the token's scopes in Developer > API credentials.
verifyHints.429: Rippling's rate limit (600 requests per 10 seconds per endpoint) was reached. Wait a few seconds and try again.

instructions:
## Rippling
This connector reads and updates **Rippling** through its REST API (`https://rest.ripplingapis.com`): workers and users, the org structure (departments, teams, work locations, levels, titles, employment types, job codes), custom fields, compensation, leave (types, balances, requests), supergroups and time entries.

**Personal data**: workers, users and compensations hold personal and pay data (names, private emails, phone numbers, home addresses, date of birth, gender, salary). Ask only for the fields the task needs, do not copy them into other systems without a reason, and give the token only the scopes the team uses.

**Setup (5 minutes)**
1. In Rippling open **Developer > API credentials** (`https://app.rippling.com/api-tokens/tokens`) and click **New API token**. You need the permission *Create and manage API Tokens*.
2. Name the token and select its **scopes**. The token can only reach data that both its scopes and the owner's permission profile allow. Pick what you use:
   - `companies.read` (required, the install check), `workers.read`, `users.read`, `departments.read`, `teams.read`, `work-locations.read`, `levels.read`, `titles.read`, `employment-types.read`, `job-codes.read`, `custom-fields.read`, `supergroups.read`.
   - `compensations.read` only if the agent should see pay.
   - `leave-types.read`, `leave-balances.read`, `leave-requests.read` (and `leave-requests.read-write` to file or approve leave).
   - `time-entries.read` (and `time-entries.read-write` to record time; needs Rippling Time).
   - `departments.read-write`, `teams.read-write`, `work-locations.read-write`, `draft-hires.read-write` for the matching writes.
3. Copy the token at once (it is shown only once) into `RIPPLING_API_TOKEN`. `rippling_list_companies` is the install check.
4. Requests run as the token's owner. A token is revoked when it stays unused for 30 days or when its owner is terminated; prefer an owner whose access is stable.

**Workflow**
- Company: `rippling_list_companies`.
- People: `rippling_list_workers` (filter by `status`, `work_email`, `user_id`, `created_at`, `updated_at`) and `rippling_get_worker`; a worker is the employment record, its `user_id` points to the login identity read with `rippling_list_users` and `rippling_get_user`. Pass `expand` (e.g. `user,manager,department`) to embed related objects in one call. Pay: `rippling_list_compensations` and `rippling_get_compensation` (the worker's `compensation_id`). Custom field definitions: `rippling_list_custom_fields`; values come with `expand=custom_fields` on workers.
- Org structure: `rippling_list_departments`, `rippling_get_department`, `rippling_list_teams`, `rippling_get_team`, `rippling_list_work_locations`, `rippling_get_work_location`, `rippling_list_levels`, `rippling_get_level`, `rippling_list_titles`, `rippling_list_employment_types`, `rippling_list_job_codes`.
- Groups: `rippling_list_supergroups`, `rippling_get_supergroup`, `rippling_list_supergroup_members`.
- Leave: `rippling_list_leave_types`, `rippling_list_leave_balances` (filter `worker_id eq '...'`), `rippling_get_leave_balance`, `rippling_list_leave_requests` (e.g. `status eq 'PENDING'`), `rippling_get_leave_request`. To book leave use `rippling_create_leave_request`; to approve, reject or cancel use `rippling_update_leave_request` with `status`.
- Time: `rippling_list_time_entries`, `rippling_get_time_entry`, `rippling_create_time_entry` (send an `idempotency_key` so a retry cannot create a duplicate), `rippling_update_time_entry`.
- Org changes: `rippling_create_department`, `rippling_update_department`, `rippling_create_team`, `rippling_update_team`, `rippling_create_work_location`, `rippling_update_work_location`.
- Hiring: `rippling_create_draft_hires` creates up to five draft hires that go through Rippling's review and approval before anyone is hired.

**Switched off at install**: `rippling_delete_team` and `rippling_delete_time_entry`; they cannot be undone, so an admin switches them on when the team needs them.

**Filters**: `filter` takes an OData-style expression on the fields each tool names: `status eq 'ACTIVE'`, `updated_at ge 2026-01-01T00:00:00`, `status in ('HIRED','ACCEPTED')`, combined with `and` / `or`. Quote strings with single quotes. At most 64 nodes per filter.

**Reading the answers**
- Lists answer `{ "results": [...], "next_link": "..." }`. Ids are 24-character hex strings.
- Dates are `YYYY-MM-DD`, timestamps ISO 8601 with offset. Money is `{ "currency_type": "USD", "value": 120000 }` in major units.
- A field the token may not see is `null` and named in `__meta.redacted_fields` with the reason; an expanded object can also be `null` for that reason. Check scopes and the owner's permissions before concluding a value is empty.
- Worker `status`: INIT, HIRED, ACCEPTED, ACTIVE, TERMINATED.

**Paging**: default 50, `limit` up to 100. When `next_link` is not null, call again with `cursor` set to the `cursor` value inside `next_link`; stop when `next_link` is null.

**Limits and errors**: 600 requests per 10 seconds per endpoint and token, then 429 (wait and retry). 400 means a bad filter, an unexpandable field or `limit` over 100; 401 a revoked or wrong token; 403 a missing scope or permission; 404 an unknown id.

tools.name: rippling_list_companies
tools.description: List the Rippling company the token belongs to (name, legal name, primary email, address, legal entities when expanded). The install check: it only needs the companies.read scope.

expand.description: Comma-separated related objects to embed instead of only their id (two levels at most, ten fields at most), e.g. "legal_entities". Expandable: legal_entities, parent_legal_entity.

order_by.description: Sort field and direction, e.g. "created_at desc" or "updated_at". Sortable fields: id, created_at, updated_at. Default ascending.

cursor.description: Opaque cursor for the next page: the cursor value inside next_link of the previous answer. Omit for the first page.

tools.name: rippling_list_workers
tools.description: List workers (employees and contractors): status, work and personal email, start and end date, title, department, manager, level, teams, location, employment type and country. Filter by status, work_email, user_id, created_at or updated_at. Contains personal data.

filter.description: OData-style filter on status, work_email, user_id, created_at, updated_at. Operators eq, ne, gt, ge, lt, le, in, and, or; quote strings with single quotes, e.g. status eq 'ACTIVE' or work_email eq 'jane@example.com' or updated_at ge 2026-01-01T00:00:00.

expand.description: Comma-separated related objects to embed instead of only their id (two levels at most, ten fields at most), e.g. "user". Expandable: user, manager, department, teams, level, employment_type, legal_entity, compensation, job_function, custom_fields, business_partners.

order_by.description: Sort field and direction, e.g. "created_at desc" or "updated_at". Sortable fields: id, created_at, updated_at. Default ascending.

cursor.description: Opaque cursor for the next page: the cursor value inside next_link of the previous answer. Omit for the first page.

expand.description: Comma-separated related objects to embed instead of only their id (two levels at most, ten fields at most), e.g. "user". Expandable: user, manager, department, teams, level, employment_type, legal_entity, compensation, job_function, custom_fields, business_partners.

start_time.description: Start time on the first day for a partial day, e.g. 13:00.

end_time.description: End time on the last day for a partial day, e.g. 12:00.

start_date_custom_hours.description: Hours off on the first day, for a partial day.

end_date_custom_hours.description: Hours off on the last day, for a partial day.

leave_type_id.description: Leave type id from rippling_list_leave_types. Give this or leave_policy_id.

leave_policy_id.description: Leave policy id. Give this or leave_type_id.

tools.name: rippling_create_time_entry
tools.description: Record worked time for a worker, as job shifts with start and end times or as a duration on a day.

worker_id.description: Worker id the time belongs to.

start_date.description: Day of a duration entry, YYYY-MM-DD.

status.description: DRAFT (default) or APPROVED; PAID and FINALIZED are set by payroll.

idempotency_key.description: Your own unique key for the entry; a second create with the same key is refused, so retries cannot duplicate it.

tools.name: rippling_update_time_entry

duration.description: Hours worked, when entering a duration instead of start and end times.

start_date.description: Day of a duration entry, YYYY-MM-DD.

status.description: DRAFT (default) or APPROVED; PAID and FINALIZED are set by payroll.

tools.name: rippling_create_draft_hires
tools.description: Create draft hires that then follow Rippling's review and approval policies before anyone is hired. Each item needs personal_info (name, invite_email), employment_info (employment_type_id, title) and work_location_info.

draft_hires.description: One to five draft hires, e.g. [{"personal_info":{"name":{"first":"Jane","last":"Doe"},"invite_email":"jane@example.com"},"employment_info":{"employment_type_id":"...","title":"Engineer","start_date":"2026-12-01T00:00:00","department_id":"...","manager_id":"..."},"work_location_info":{"location_id":"..."}}]. Ids come from rippling_list_employment_types, rippling_list_departments, rippling_list_workers and rippling_list_work_locations.
